subject: Redwood marketplace procurement: PO vs card & AWS/GCP/Azure interest
messages:

Cc: procurement@lumenai.com

Subject: Redwood discovery recap + procurement questions

Hi Sara / Alex —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a few procurement questions to help us map the commercial path:

Key points from the call:
- Primary use: production inference for LumenAI Recommendations (real-time scoring, 50–200 reqs/sec at peak).
- Expected monthly token volume (generation + embedding): ~50M–120M tokens depending on adoption.
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for the majority of requests; some background batch workloads acceptable at higher latency.

Procurement/commercial questions:
1) Payment method preference: do you prefer to purchase via Purchase Order (PO) or via company card for initial pilots? Any existing threshold that forces PO (e.g., > $50k)?
2) Marketplace interest: would purchasing via AWS/GCP/Azure Marketplace be preferred? Marketplaces can speed procurement and centralize billing in some orgs.
3) Contract cadence/timeline: target date to have billing mechanism agreed? Are you planning a short pilot (1–3 months) before a committed Reserved/Dedicated purchase?

I attached a short "marketplace procurement checklist" and a one-page SOC 2 summary for procurement to review. If it helps, I can loop in our sales ops/finance folks to walk through PO paperwork vs Marketplace contract differences.

Next steps: if you can share your procurement lead (or confirm Alex as point of contact), we can schedule a 30-min procurement walkthrough early next week.

Appreciate it —

Camila Reyes

Hi Camila —

Great summary, thanks. A few quick answers from our side:

- Payment method: For pilots under $25k we can usually do a corporate card. Anything above ~ $50k requires a PO and standard procurement review.
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is our preferred route when available — it speeds vendor onboarding and centralizes billing through our cloud purchasing process. We occasionally use GCP marketplace but our buying org is primarily AWS-aligned.
- Timeline: We are aiming to make a decision in Q2; procurement review would start as soon as we have a ballpark estimate.

I’m CC’ing Alex (ops/procurement) on this thread — Alex will own the PO review. Alex, I’m forwarding Camila’s checklist and SOC 2 summary for your team. I’ve attached our PO template in case that helps (see attached).

Thanks —

Hi Sara / Alex —

Perfect — that's really helpful context. A few notes on the commercial paths so you can weigh options with procurement:

1) Card (pilot): quickest route to get started (same-day for card approvals). Good for proof-of-concept or early pilot where spend is expected to stay modest.

2) PO / Direct contract: standard for committed spending and Reserved/Dedicated capacity. Our sales ops team will sign a Master Subscription Agreement and SOW; PO references to our invoice number work fine.

3) Marketplace (AWS preferred): if you purchase via AWS Marketplace (SaaS or metered), procurement can buy through their existing cloud contracting process. Benefits: faster procurement approval in many orgs, consolidated billing on the AWS invoice, and the option to subscribe via Marketplace listing. Caveats: Marketplace pricing/discounting and reserved capacity commitments are handled slightly differently — we can provide both Marketplace listing details and a direct-contract quote so you have both options.

Attached: marketplace-pricing-estimate.pdf (ballpark based on the volumes discussed) and a short "Marketplace onboarding steps" doc that outlines typical timelines and required PO/contract language.

Next steps I propose:
- Schedule 30-min call with Alex + your procurement to walk through the PO template vs AWS Marketplace workflow (please suggest availability).
- Monica (cc) will prepare a short technical/ops note for procurement about network/security controls for Marketplace vs Dedicated deployments.
- Aditya (cc) will prepare a draft commercial summary and SOW template to accelerate PO review.

Proposed times: Fri 20 Feb 10:00 AM PT / Mon 23 Feb 9:00 AM PT — let us know what works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks again — we’ll stand by to help with whichever path you prefer.

Best,
Camila Reyes
